lines.text: GTA 6 is out today. So how do open world games show a giant world with no loading screens?
The whole world won't fit in your console's memory. So games don't load it all at once.
Instead, the map is split into chunks. Only the chunks around you are kept in memory.
As you move, the game quietly loads chunks ahead of you from storage, and throws away the ones behind.
Far away things use simpler versions of models, with fewer details. You'd never notice from a distance.
On fast SSDs, games can fetch what they need just a second or so before you need it.
That's why speed is the real stress test: move fast enough, and the world must load faster than you arrive.
